newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium backs Dutch plan to study kerosene tax.
newsitem.headline: Belgium backs Dutch plan to study kerosene tax.

text.p: Belgian Transport Minister Michel Daerden said on Wednesday Belgium would back Dutch plans for a European Union feasibility study into taxing kerosene fuel used in air transport.

"Belgium supports the Netherlands on the project to do a feasibility study into such a tax...but we have to be conscious of the complexities of the subject," Daerden told a Belgian parliamentary committee meeting.
The Netherlands presently holds the presidency of the European Union, which has long mulled such a tax.

Daerden noted that changing the zero rate on kerosene used in international flights - something which was agreed as long ago as 1944 - was probably impossible in the near future, given the number of countries that would have to be consulted and the number of treaties that would have to be ratified.
He said, however, if the zero rate was to be changed Belgium would favour another commonly-agreed rate. "Otherwise there would be a permanent distortion of competition between airlines," he said.
